reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Statewide Court Automation Fund establishment and revenue sources
headings.reviewNote: Establishes Statewide Court Automation Fund, crediting surcharge revenues and gifts, non-reverting to general revenue.

headings.title: Court automation committee composition and member reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Delineates 25-member court automation committee composition (15 judicial/staff appointees, 2 bar, 4 legislative, 4 ex officio), two-year terms, and actual expense reimbursements.

headings.title: Statewide court automation system development and consultant authority
headings.reviewNote: Directs committee to develop and maintain statewide court automation system, authorizes hiring consultants and purchasing goods/services, and permits pilot projects.

headings.title: Hardware and software competitive bidding thresholds and specifications
headings.reviewNote: Requires lowest and best bid via office of administration for hardware and software purchases exceeding five thousand dollars.

headings.title: Restrictions on mandatory operating system changes for circuit courts
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits requiring circuit court operating system changes unless committee provides personnel, funds, and equipment, and requires prior approval for reimbursement.

headings.title: Security and privacy standards for confidential judicial records
headings.reviewNote: Mandates strict security and privacy standards by supreme court rule, making knowing confidential record release a class B misdemeanor and use for financial gain a class E felony.

headings.title: Annual electronic progress reports to legislative committee chairs
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual electronic progress report by January fifteenth to legislative budget and judiciary committee chairs.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 7 subsections; corrected committee member count to 25 and aligned mandatory/permissive phrasing and financial-gain felony note.

headings.title: Municipal court automation ordinances and state agreement terms
headings.reviewNote: Permits municipal court automation via local surcharge ordinance (citing *476.053, transferred to 488.027) and agreement with state courts administrator.

headings.title: Duration of municipal surcharges and exemption from fund transfers
headings.reviewNote: Allows municipal surcharge duration beyond circuit court limits and exempts special municipal automation funds from section 33.080.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections and footnote noting section 476.053 was transferred to section 488.027 in 2000.

headings.title: Projected fee collections and fee adjustments for training fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs state courts administrator to project fee collections (noting *488.023 was repealed in 2000) and permits fee adjustments under section 488.015.

headings.title: Judicial personnel training and education fund creation and transfer cap
headings.reviewNote: Establishes training fund in state treasury with annual general revenue transfers capped at two percent of personal services.

headings.title: Segregation and use of dedicated training fee receipts and grants
headings.reviewNote: Requires depositing training fees and grants into the fund, mandating segregation for specific purposes.

headings.title: Fund disbursement authority and definition of judicial personnel
headings.reviewNote: Directs treasurer disbursements to state courts administrator and defines judicial personnel to include court staff and judges.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections and footnote noting section 488.023 was repealed in 2000; preserved permissive fee adjustment phrasing.

headings.title: Definition of court personnel excluding judicial officers
headings.reviewNote: Defines court personnel across all state court divisions, clerks, and reporters, explicitly excluding judges.

headings.title: State Court Administration Revolving Fund creation and revenue sources
headings.reviewNote: Creates State Court Administration Revolving Fund in state treasury for training and education registration fees, grants, and other receipts.

headings.title: Transcript preparation receipts and purpose segregation in fund
headings.reviewNote: Deposits court transcript preparation fees, grants, and other receipts into the fund and mandates segregation of moneys collected for a particular purpose.

headings.title: Treasurer administration and disbursements for training and transcripts
headings.reviewNote: Directs state treasurer to administer the fund and disburse appropriated moneys to state courts administrator for court personnel training and court transcript preparation.

headings.title: Biennial non-reversion threshold for revolving fund balance
headings.reviewNote: Exempts unexpended biennial fund balances from section 33.080 general revenue transfer up to the greater of half of prior-year expenditures or fifty thousand dollars.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections; replaced mismatched headings on subsections 3-5 and corrected subsection 2 note to match transcript receipts, disbursements, and biennial non-reversion.

headings.title: Appointment and duties of circuit court marshals in correctional circuits
headings.reviewNote: Permits presiding judge in circuits with qualifying DOC inmate populations or a DOC diagnostic/reception center and DMH chapter 552/SORTS facility to appoint a marshal.

headings.title: Marshal salary limitations and payment from state or federal funds
headings.reviewNote: Caps marshal salary at ninety percent of highest paid sheriff in circuit and mandates payment from state or federal funds.

headings.title: Marshal qualification standards, training, and law enforcement powers
headings.reviewNote: Requires five years law enforcement experience, federal marshal training, and authorizes process service, firearms, and arrests.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections covering marshal appointment in qualifying DOC and DMH/SORTS circuits, salary cap, and law enforcement powers.

headings.title: Short title as Judicial Privacy Act
headings.reviewNote: Cites sections 476.1300 to 476.1313 as the Judicial Privacy Act.

headings.title: Definitions under Judicial Privacy Act
headings.reviewNote: Defines court-related officer (noting S.B. 218 original-rolls wording "supreme court of Missouri"), government agency, home address, immediate family, personal information, and written request.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections and original-rolls note on S.B. 218 wording ("supreme court of Missouri").

headings.title: Government agency duty to remove protected personal information upon request
headings.reviewNote: Requires government agencies to remove officer personal info within five business days of written request, exempting it from sunshine law.

headings.title: Injunctive relief and attorney fee awards for agency noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes civil actions for injunctive or declaratory relief and attorney fee awards upon agency noncompliance.

headings.title: Exemption for state highway patrol and court automation records
headings.reviewNote: Exempts section 43.020 highway patrol entities and statewide court automation proceedings governed by supreme court rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections; noted catchline refers to "state agency" while body applies broadly to "government agency" with highway patrol and court automation exemptions.

headings.title: Prohibition on internet posting of personal information after written request
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits persons, businesses, or associations from posting court-related officer personal information on internet after written request.

headings.title: Prohibition on selling or trading personal information for tampering or threats
headings.reviewNote: Bars soliciting, selling, or trading personal information on internet to tamper with officers or threaten health and safety.

headings.title: Application to online directories, search engines, and data aggregators
headings.reviewNote: Applies prohibitions specifically to internet phone directories, search engines, data aggregators, and service providers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections barring internet posting after written request and soliciting, selling, or trading personal information for tampering or threats.

headings.title: Five-day deadline to remove personal information from the internet
headings.reviewNote: Gives any person, business, or association five business days after receiving a written privacy request to remove protected personal information from the internet.

headings.title: Duty to keep personal information off controlled websites
headings.reviewNote: Requires any person, business, or association receiving a written request to ensure personal information is unavailable on controlled or subsidiary websites.

headings.title: Prohibition on disclosing personal information to third parties through any medium
headings.reviewNote: Bars making personal information available to any other person, business, or association through any medium after notice.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections; broadened subsections 1-2 titles from "commercial" to match statutory scope covering any person, business, or association.

headings.title: Receipt of valid written request required for violation finding
headings.reviewNote: Absolves agencies and entities of liability absent receipt of a valid written request.

headings.title: Requirements for valid direct or supreme court clerk written request
headings.reviewNote: Specifies validity standards for direct written requests or centralized supreme court clerk notification procedures.

headings.title: Quarterly distribution of protected officer list by supreme court clerk
headings.reviewNote: Requires quarterly transmission of protected officer lists to agency supervisory authorities, constituting written notice.

headings.title: Submission of written requests by chief clerks on officer behalf
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes chief clerks or circuit clerks to submit written requests on officer behalf upon written consent.

headings.title: Required contents and immediate family designations in written requests
headings.reviewNote: Specifies required request contents, secondary residence designations, and identification of immediate family members.

headings.title: Duration of written request until officer consent or death
headings.reviewNote: Provides that written requests remain valid until written release consent and expire upon officer death.

headings.title: Exemption for constitutional and statutory campaign and ethics disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Exempts disclosures required by constitutional campaign finance provisions, ethics statutes, and chapter 130.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 7 subsections governing written privacy request validity, quarterly clerk lists, chief clerk submissions, duration, and campaign/ethics exemptions.

headings.title: Recorder of deeds compliance with Judicial Privacy Act
headings.reviewNote: Governs recorder of deeds compliance with sections 476.1300 to 476.1310 under specific section standards.

headings.title: Definitions of eligible documents, indexes, shielding, and requests
headings.reviewNote: Defines eligible documents, indexes, recorder of deeds, shielding, and written request for land records.

headings.title: Information required in shielding requests transmitted to recorder of deeds
headings.reviewNote: Requires county-specific document locator numbers, legal names, aliases, and family member details in shielding requests.

headings.title: Five-day recorder shielding duty and reply for missing locator numbers
headings.reviewNote: Mandates shielding of eligible documents within five business days and electronic reply for unlocated document numbers.

headings.title: Discrepancy notice and delay of shielding for unlisted names
headings.reviewNote: Permits delay of shielding pending clerk confirmation where requesting names do not appear on instrument.

headings.title: Presentation of shielding request copy for subsequent recorded documents
headings.reviewNote: Requires officers to present request copy at time of recording to secure shielding within five business days.

headings.title: Duration of document shielding until court order or notarized affidavit
headings.reviewNote: Maintains document shielding until receipt of court order or notarized termination affidavit from officer.

headings.title: Permitted access to shielded documents by instrument parties or by court order
headings.reviewNote: Allows access to shielded documents by parties to instrument or upon court order or notarized affidavit.

headings.title: Immunity for recorder of deeds acting in good faith
headings.reviewNote: Protects recorders of deeds from liability for good faith compliance efforts and prior unshielded releases.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 9 subsections governing recorder of deeds electronic shielding duties, five-day timelines, name discrepancies, access exceptions, and good-faith immunity.

headings.title: Formulation of state judicial department budget under reorganization act
headings.reviewNote: Directs formulation of the state judicial department budget under section 1(6)(4) of the Omnibus State Reorganization Act of 1974 and section 33.220 unless otherwise provided.

headings.title: Supreme court as department head and appellate or circuit budget estimates
headings.reviewNote: Designates supreme court as department head and directs appellate chief judges and circuit presiding judges, with majority judicial approval, to present estimates like executive divisions.

headings.title: October first deadline to submit judicial budget estimates to budget director
headings.reviewNote: Requires judicial department budget estimates to be provided to the budget director on or before October first each year preceding the annual legislative session.

headings.title: Budget submission by circuit and district with contingency appropriations
headings.reviewNote: Specifies budget format by circuit and district while permitting flexible contingency allocations by supreme court.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections; replaced inaccurate headings on subsections 1-3 to match Reorganization Act formulation, supreme court/division estimates, and October 1 budget director deadline.

headings.title: Executive council composition and election of judicial conference members
headings.reviewNote: Defines composition of judicial conference executive council, including appellate, circuit, associate, probate, and retired members.

headings.title: Supervisory authority of executive council and election of vice president
headings.reviewNote: Grants executive council general supervision over conference work and provides for election of vice president.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections detailing judicial conference executive council membership, election, terms, supervision, and vice president.

headings.title: Judicial conference and executive council study of judicial system
headings.reviewNote: Directs the judicial conference and its executive council to study judicial organization, rules, procedures, practice, work accomplished, and administrative problems.

headings.title: Mandatory docket and caseload reports by presiding and chief judges
headings.reviewNote: Requires presiding and chief judges to submit docket and business reports to council as public records.

headings.title: Biennial legislative recommendations on practice codes and constitutional rulings
headings.reviewNote: Directs council to submit biennial recommendations to general assembly regarding practice codes and unconstitutional statutes.

headings.title: Conference authority to appoint committees and adopt internal rules
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes appointment of committees and adoption of rules necessary to carry out conference duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections; aligned subsection 1 title to cover both the judicial conference and executive council.

headings.title: Associate circuit judge fine schedule committee and county adoption
headings.reviewNote: Permits supreme court to appoint associate circuit judge committee to set traffic/minor offense fine schedules (noting *210.104 repealed in 2006) and lets counties adopt schedules and bureau participation.

headings.title: Offenses excluded from fine schedules
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits fine schedules from including offenses involving personal injury or property damage, DWI/DUI, counterfeited/suspended/revoked licenses, or fleeing an officer.

headings.title: Establishment of centralized violations bureau and court cost collection
headings.reviewNote: Mandates a centralized bureau established by supreme court rule to accept guilty or not guilty pleas, fine payments, and all originating-court costs.

headings.title: Guilty plea, trial waiver, and driver improvement upon fine payment
headings.reviewNote: Provides that payment of fine to bureau constitutes guilty plea, conviction, and consent to driver improvement course.

headings.title: Not guilty plea submission and referral to local prosecutor for trial
headings.reviewNote: Governs not guilty pleas sent to bureau, referral to prosecutor, and trial setting in local court.

headings.title: Required written notice of fines, costs, and appearance obligations
headings.reviewNote: Mandates written notice to defendants concerning fine amounts, court costs, and failure to appear consequences.

headings.title: Non-state trust status of bureau receipts and investment revolving fund
headings.reviewNote: Classifies bureau collections as trust funds, directing interest into judicial administration revolving fund.

headings.title: Failure to appear penalties and driver license suspension notice
headings.reviewNote: Subjects non-appearing defendants to failure to appear charges under section 544.665 and license suspension under section 302.341.

headings.title: Use of statutory court cost collection remedies for bureau assessments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes bureau and courts to utilize collection remedies under sections 488.010 to 488.020 for unpaid fines and costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 9 subsections and repealed section 210.104 note; replaced shifted/mismatched headings on subsections 1-3 covering fine committee, excluded offenses, and centralized bureau.

headings.title: Annual judicial salary adjustments within appropriation limits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes annual salary adjustments for designated judicial officers capped by executive pay plan adjustments.

headings.title: Line item appropriation requirement and inclusion in statutory salary
headings.reviewNote: Requires separate line item appropriation for salary adjustments, integrating approved adjustments into statutory salary.

headings.title: Annual compensation schedule maintenance and revisor notes
headings.reviewNote: Directs office of administration to maintain compensation index and revisor of statutes to annotate statutory sections.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections covering annual judicial salary adjustments, line-item appropriations, and office of administration/revisor schedule duties.

headings.title: Prohibition on dividing securities into nonnegotiable increments
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits courts from dividing securities among multiple recipients in a manner rendering negotiable securities nonnegotiable.

headings.title: Division into allowable tradeable amounts and alternative distribution remedies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes division into allowable tradeable amounts, unequal distributions with offsets, liquidation, or other remedies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections barring division of negotiable securities into nonnegotiable increments and permitting tradeable-amount or alternative remedies.

headings.title: Retirement eligibility and appointment of special commissioners at age sixty-five
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes special commissioner appointments and fifty percent compensation for judges retiring at age 65 after 12 years service.

headings.title: Pre-June 30, 1988 special commissioner election for supreme court judges
headings.reviewNote: Permits qualifying supreme court judges (age 65 with 8 years or age 60 with 12 years) to elect before June 30, 1988, to become special commissioners at half salary.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections; replaced mismatched subsection 2 heading to accurately reflect pre-June 30, 1988 supreme court judge special commissioner election.

headings.title: Retirement rights of non-attorney judges and constitutional court officers
headings.reviewNote: Extends section 476.450 retirement rights to non-attorney judges and constitutional court judges serving twelve years by October 13, 1969.

headings.title: Inclusion of justice of the peace service in judicial tenure calculation
headings.reviewNote: Allows magistrate and probate judges to include justice of the peace service in computing prior judicial service.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections extending section 476.450 retirement rights to non-attorney and constitutional court judges and crediting justice of the peace service.

headings.title: Retirement age of seventy for magistrate and probate judges
headings.reviewNote: Sets retirement age of seventy for magistrate and probate judges, permitting completion of elected terms.

headings.title: Commission on retirement petition to serve until age seventy-six
headings.reviewNote: Allows eligible judges to petition retirement commission to continue serving until age seventy-six to complete twelve years.

headings.title: Completion of unexpired terms for magistrates elected in 1976
headings.reviewNote: Permits magistrates elected in 1976 to fill unexpired terms to complete their terms regardless of age.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections and case annotation (O'Neil v. Baine, 568 S.W.2d 761) on age-70 retirement, age-76 extension petitions, and 1976 magistrate terms.

headings.title: Disqualification from retirement for felony conviction or impeachment
headings.reviewNote: Disqualifies persons convicted of a felony or impeached/removed for moral turpitude from judicial retirement benefits.

headings.title: Suspension and forfeiture of benefits for beneficiary charged with killing judge
headings.reviewNote: Requires suspension and forfeiture of benefits for any beneficiary charged with or convicted of intentionally killing a judge.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections covering felony/impeachment disqualification and benefit suspension/forfeiture for beneficiaries charged with killing a judge.

headings.title: Definitions of beneficiary, benefit, judge, and salary
headings.reviewNote: Defines beneficiary, benefit, commissioner of administration, judge, and salary under judicial retirement system.

headings.title: Restoration of beneficiary rights for surviving spouses remarrying before October 1, 1984
headings.reviewNote: Restores beneficiary rights for surviving spouses whose benefits terminated upon remarriage prior to October 1, 1984.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections defining judicial retirement terms and restoring beneficiary rights for surviving spouses remarried before October 1, 1984.

headings.title: Retirement eligibility at age sixty-two with twelve years judicial service
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes retirement benefits at age 62 with 12 years service, and mandates retirement at age 70 under constitution.

headings.title: Retirement eligibility at age sixty with fifteen years judicial service
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes retirement benefits at age sixty with an aggregate of fifteen years of judicial service.

headings.title: Retirement eligibility at age fifty-five with twenty years service and special consultants
headings.reviewNote: Permits retirement at age 55 with 20 years service, appointment of pre-1999 terminators as consultants, and COLA limits.

headings.title: Special retirement consultants for judges terminating before August 13, 1988
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes MOSERS appointment of pre-August 13, 1988 retirees as special consultants on retirement and aging.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections covering age/service retirement thresholds (62/12, 60/15, 55/20), age-70 mandatory retirement, and special retirement consultants.

headings.title: Applicability to judges first taking office on or after January 1, 2011
headings.reviewNote: Applies special retirement provisions to judges first taking office on or after January 1, 2011, noting *476.445 was repealed in 2014.

headings.title: Normal retirement at age sixty-seven and proportional reduced annuities
headings.reviewNote: Establishes normal retirement at age 67 with 12 years service and reduced proportional annuities for shorter tenure.

headings.title: Early retirement at age sixty-two with twenty years judicial service
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes early retirement at age 62 with 20 years service and proportional reduced benefits for shorter tenure.

headings.title: Mandatory constitutional retirement age of seventy years
headings.reviewNote: Enforces mandatory constitutional retirement at age seventy for judges under this section.

headings.title: Inapplicability of prior service credit and post-retirement COLA sections
headings.reviewNote: Exempts post-2011 judges from sections 104.344, 476.524, and 476.690.

headings.title: Four percent employee contribution pickup, account interest, and refund rules
headings.reviewNote: Mandates four percent employer-picked-up employee contributions, T-bill interest rates, and post-termination refund rules.

headings.title: Legislative amendment and alteration of future employee contribution rates
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes legislative alteration of contribution rates and benefits solely for prospective judicial service.

headings.title: Suspension of retirement compensation during active public or judicial employment
headings.reviewNote: Suspends retirement payments during active MOSERS employment or judicial service, preserving senior judge service.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 8 subsections and repealed section 476.445 note governing post-2011 judge retirement ages, 4% picked-up contributions, T-bill interest, and reemployment suspension.

headings.title: Optional reduced survivor annuity options for post-2011 judges
headings.reviewNote: Establishes four optional reduced survivor annuity options for judges first employed on or after January 1, 2011.

headings.title: Mandatory spousal option selection absent written spousal consent
headings.reviewNote: Mandates election of option 1 or 2 for married judges unless spouse consents in writing to another payment form.

headings.title: Cancellation of survivor option and reversion upon predecease of spouse
headings.reviewNote: Permits cancellation of survivor option and return to unreduced annuity if spouse dies after annuity starting date.

headings.title: Continuation of survivor option benefits following marriage dissolution
headings.reviewNote: Maintains designated former spouse survivor eligibility notwithstanding subsequent dissolution of marriage.

headings.title: Post-retirement survivor option election upon subsequent marriage
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes survivor option election within one year of marriage for judges who remarry or were previously ineligible.

headings.title: Modification of option selection prior to initial annuity disbursement
headings.reviewNote: Allows judges to change retirement option elections prior to the mailing or electronic transfer of the first payment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections covering optional reduced survivor annuities (Options 1-4), spousal consent, reversion on spouse death, dissolution, and post-retirement marriage elections.

headings.title: Survivor benefits for judge dying in office or on long-term disability
headings.reviewNote: Provides 50 percent monthly survivor benefits upon death of an active judge or long-term disabled former judge, with proportional reduction referencing repealed *Const. Art. V § 30.

headings.title: Survivor benefits for unretired former judge with twelve years service
headings.reviewNote: Provides 50 percent monthly survivor benefits upon death of a former judge with 12 years of service who left office after September 28, 1971, without retiring or withdrawing contributions.

headings.title: Survivor benefits upon death of retired judge receiving retirement compensation
headings.reviewNote: Provides 50 percent monthly survivor benefits upon the death of a retired judge receiving retirement compensation under sections 476.515 to 476.570 (**476.570 repealed in 1978).

headings.title: Preservation of existing survivor benefits payable on or before August 12, 1974
headings.reviewNote: Protects survivor benefits being paid or accrued on or before August 12, 1974, from alteration.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections and repealed reference notes (*Const. Art. V § 30, **476.570); refined subsection 1 and replaced inaccurate subsection 2 heading for unretired former judges.

headings.title: Special consultant appointment for surviving spouse of judge serving twenty-five years
headings.reviewNote: Appoints surviving spouses of judges serving 25 years as special consultants receiving half of special commissioner pay.

headings.title: Special consultant appointment for surviving spouse of judge dying after January 1, 1989
headings.reviewNote: Appoints surviving spouses of post-1989 deceased judges with 11 years service as special consultants on retirement.

headings.title: Special consultant for spouse of disabled judge dying on or after January 1, 1994
headings.reviewNote: Appoints surviving spouses of long-term disabled judges dying on or after January 1, 1994, as special consultants with benefits increased to 50 percent of section 476.530 compensation.

headings.title: Exemption of special consultant compensation from process and assignment
headings.reviewNote: Exempts consultant compensation from execution, garnishment, attachment, sequestration, and assignment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections on surviving spouse special consultant appointments and process/assignment exemption; corrected subsection 3 date scope to "on or after January 1, 1994".

headings.title: Proportional early retirement compensation at age sixty-two
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes reduced early retirement compensation at age 62 proportional to service under 12 years.

headings.title: Proportional early retirement compensation at age sixty
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes reduced early retirement compensation at age 60 proportional to service under 15 years.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections governing proportional reduced early retirement compensation at ages 62 and 60.

headings.title: Termination of payroll deductions for retirement benefits after September 1, 1976
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits payroll deductions for judicial retirement benefits after September 1, 1976.

headings.title: Refund of pre-1976 retirement contributions and interest upon retirement
headings.reviewNote: Directs commissioner of administration to refund pre-1976 contributions with interest upon retirement or upon request after leaving office without retirement eligibility.

headings.title: Refund of pre-1976 contributions and interest to surviving beneficiary
headings.reviewNote: Provides payment of unrefunded pre-1976 contributions with interest to designated beneficiary or estate upon judge death.

headings.title: Written request for ninety-day cash refund of pre-1976 contributions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes written request for lump-sum refund of pre-1976 contributions and interest within 90 days without loss of benefits.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections ending post-September 1, 1976 retirement payroll deductions and governing pre-1976 contribution refunds.

headings.title: Special commissioner election for judges receiving full retirement benefits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes judges receiving section 476.530 benefits to elect lifetime appointment as special commissioners at full compensation.

headings.title: Special commissioner election for judges receiving reduced early retirement benefits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes judges receiving section 476.545 benefits to elect appointment as special commissioners at proportional compensation.

headings.title: Statutory provisions governing special commissioners and cessation of general benefits
headings.reviewNote: Applies designated commissioner statutes and terminates general retirement system applicability upon election.

headings.title: Lump sum refund of retirement contributions upon special commissioner election
headings.reviewNote: Permits lump-sum refund of retirement contributions under sections 476.515 to 476.570 (*476.570 repealed in 1978) upon written application after electing special commissioner status.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections and repealed section 476.570 note governing special commissioner elections and lump-sum contribution refunds.

headings.title: Cost-of-living adjustments for special retirement consultants
headings.reviewNote: Provides 4 to 5 percent annual cost-of-living increases capped at 65 percent of initial benefit for special consultants.

headings.title: Supplemental annual cost-of-living adjustments after reaching initial cap
headings.reviewNote: Establishes supplemental CPI benefit increases up to five percent annually after reaching the 65 percent cap.

headings.title: Annual cost-of-living adjustments for judges employed after August 28, 1997
headings.reviewNote: Entitles judges first employed on or after August 28, 1997, to annual CPI adjustments capped at five percent.

headings.title: Survivor eligibility for annual cost-of-living adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Extends annual cost-of-living benefit increases to survivors of judges employed on or after August 28, 1997.

headings.title: Monthly installment payments and consolidation with retirement benefits
headings.reviewNote: Directs cost-of-living compensation to be paid in equal monthly installments consolidated with retirement benefits.

headings.title: Exemption of consolidated retirement benefits from legal process and assignment
headings.reviewNote: Exempts consolidated retirement compensation from execution, garnishment, attachment, sequestration, and assignment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections governing special consultant COLAs, supplemental post-cap increases, post-August 28, 1997 judge and survivor COLAs, and process exemption.

headings.title: Canvassing and certification of county nonpartisan court plan election abstracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires election boards to count, canvass, and return separate abstract sheets on nonpartisan court plan to secretary of state.

headings.title: Gubernatorial proclamation of nonpartisan court plan adoption
headings.reviewNote: Directs secretary of state canvass in governor's presence and gubernatorial proclamation declaring nonpartisan plan adopted.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on canvassing and gubernatorial proclamation of nonpartisan court plan elections; noted catchline parenthetical "(Clay County)" does not appear in body text.

headings.title: Application for senior judge or senior commissioner service
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes retired judges to apply annually with supreme court clerk for senior judge service, including health evaluations.

headings.title: Appointment of senior judges by supreme court based on caseload and need
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes supreme court to appoint senior judges for up to one year based on caseload, need, and commission reports.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections governing retired senior judge/commissioner annual applications and supreme court appointments based on caseload and need.

headings.title: Per diem compensation calculation and annual earnings cap for senior judges
headings.reviewNote: Sets per diem compensation at fifty percent of daily active salary, capping total annual earnings at full active salary.

headings.title: Travel and subsistence reimbursement for senior judges
headings.reviewNote: Entitles senior judges and commissioners assigned outside their county of residence to reimbursement for travel and other actual and necessary expenses.

headings.title: Monthly senior judge service certification and payment warrants
headings.reviewNote: Requires senior judges to certify prior-month service and expenses to state courts administrator by the 10th of each month for warrant issuance and month-end treasurer payment.

headings.title: Monthly MOSERS certification and retirement credit for senior service
headings.reviewNote: Requires state courts administrator to certify senior service monthly to MOSERS by the 20th, granting one year of judicial credit per 235 days and recalculating benefits upon reaching 12 years.

headings.title: Ineligibility for senior judge benefits during private law practice
headings.reviewNote: Bars any person engaged in the private practice of law or doing a law business from receiving benefits under this section notwithstanding sections 476.510 or 476.565.

headings.title: Annual judicial conference report on senior judge usage and costs
headings.reviewNote: Directs Missouri judicial conference to report annually on senior judges assigned, cases assigned and disposed of, and related expenditures.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections; replaced mismatched headings on subsections 3, 5, and 6 and refined subsection 4 to match monthly certifications, MOSERS credit, private practice bar, and annual report.

headings.title: Cost-of-living credit accrual during continued service beyond retirement eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Adds accrued cost-of-living increases between retirement eligibility and actual retirement, subject to sixty-five percent cap.

headings.title: Special consultant appointment for judges retiring between 1995 and 1996
headings.reviewNote: Appoints judges retiring between 1995 and 1996 as special consultants to recalculate benefits under subsection 1.

headings.title: Special consultant appointment and benefit recalculation for pre-1995 retirees
headings.reviewNote: Appoints pre-1995 retirees receiving benefits in 2000 as special consultants to recalculate benefits prospectively.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections governing accrued COLA credits for judges continuing past retirement eligibility and special consultant recalculations.

headings.title: Mandatory auxiliary aids and services for deaf persons in legal proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Requires designated authorities to provide qualified interpreters and auxiliary aids in civil, criminal, and detention hearings.

headings.title: Inadmissibility of statements obtained from deaf persons prior to interpreter
headings.reviewNote: Bars admissibility of statements obtained from involuntarily detained or arrested deaf persons before requested aids are provided, and bars holding otherwise-releasable deaf arrestees.

headings.title: Appointment and payment of interpreters for indigent deaf criminal defendants
headings.reviewNote: Mandates provision and public payment of interpreters for indigent deaf persons to assist counsel in criminal defenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections, cross-reference to section 490.722, and State v. Wilson (169 S.W.3d 571) annotation on deaf auxiliary aids, statement inadmissibility, and indigent defense.

headings.title: Privileged communications between deaf persons, counsel, and auxiliary providers
headings.reviewNote: Protects communications through auxiliary aids under attorney-client privilege, immunizing providers from compelled testimony.

headings.title: Spatial positioning and sightline requirements for auxiliary providers
headings.reviewNote: Bars commencing proceedings until auxiliary providers are positioned in full view to assure proper communication.

headings.title: Written waiver of auxiliary aids and approval of counsel
headings.reviewNote: Requires knowing, voluntary written waiver approved by counsel or authority, barring waiver by mere failure to request.

headings.title: Reasonable fees, travel expenses, and subsistence for auxiliary providers
headings.reviewNote: Entitles auxiliary providers to reasonable fees, travel, and subsistence based on deaf commission fee schedules.

headings.title: Payment of auxiliary provider fees from state courts administrator funds
headings.reviewNote: Directs payment of auxiliary aids fees and expenses in court proceedings from state courts administrator appropriations.

headings.title: Prohibition on assessing interpreter costs against deaf persons or proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Bars assessing costs of interpreters or auxiliary aids against deaf persons or taxing costs to the proceeding.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections governing privileged deaf communications, provider sightline positioning, written waivers, fees/expenses, OSCA payment, and cost-assessment bar.

headings.title: Commission list of qualified interpreters and replacement authority
headings.reviewNote: Requires authorities to request interpreter lists from commission and permits appointing replacements to meet deaf person needs.

headings.title: Compliance directives issued by deaf commission and assistive technology council
headings.reviewNote: Directs commission for deaf and assistive technology council to issue compliance directives and standards for public authorities.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections governing qualified interpreter lists, replacement authority, and compliance directives by the deaf commission and assistive technology council.

headings.title: Missouri CASA Fund establishment and funding sources
headings.reviewNote: Creates Missouri CASA Fund in state treasury to support court-appointed special advocate programs statewide.

headings.title: Investment of CASA fund balances and credit of interest earnings
headings.reviewNote: Directs state treasurer to invest CASA fund moneys with all investment earnings credited back to the fund.

headings.title: Administration and disbursement of CASA funds by state courts administrator
headings.reviewNote: Directs state courts administrator to fund start-up programs, allocate base rates, and enforce national CASA affiliation.

headings.title: Exemption of Missouri CASA Fund from biennial general revenue transfer
headings.reviewNote: Exempts unexpended balances in CASA fund from biennial transfer to general revenue under section 33.080.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections establishing, investing, disbursing, and exempting the Missouri CASA Fund from biennial general revenue reversion.

headings.title: Permissive fingerprint requirement for court interpreter certification
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes office of state courts administrator to require fingerprint submissions as part of qualified court interpreter certification applications under section 476.800.

headings.title: State and federal fingerprint criminal history checks through highway patrol
headings.reviewNote: Directs state courts administrator to submit interpreter fingerprints to state highway patrol for state and federal background checks.

headings.title: Criminal history record searches and administrator access to records
headings.reviewNote: Governs central repository and FBI records searches, granting state courts administrator full access to discovered criminal records.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections; adjusted subsection 1 title to preserve permissive "may require" for interpreter certification fingerprint submissions.

headings.title: Mandatory interpreter appointment for non-English speaking parties or witnesses
headings.reviewNote: Mandates court appointment of qualified interpreters and translators in all legal proceedings where a non-English speaking person is a party or witness.

headings.title: Prior notice requirements for parties needing interpreter services
headings.reviewNote: Requires non-English speaking parties or parties calling non-English witnesses to provide timely prior notice to the court.

headings.title: Appointment of interpreters for non-English speaking parents in juvenile cases
headings.reviewNote: Directs appointment of qualified interpreters to assist non-English speaking parents, guardians, or custodians of juveniles.

headings.title: Knowing waiver and retraction of right to qualified interpreter
headings.reviewNote: Permits court acceptance of knowing, intelligent waiver of interpreter right and allows non-English speaking persons to retract waiver.

headings.title: Interpreter oath, standard of true interpretation, and advice prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Requires interpreter oath of true interpretation and prohibits giving legal advice, explanations, or personal opinions.

headings.title: Attorney-client privilege protection for interpreters and translators
headings.reviewNote: Protects information conveyed to interpreters or translators under attorney-client privilege, barring compelled testimony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections; broadened subsection 1 title to include both parties and witnesses alongside notice, juvenile parents, waivers, oath, and privilege.

headings.title: Reasonable fees and travel expenses for interpreters and translators
headings.reviewNote: Allows court-approved reasonable fees and state travel expenses for interpreters, excluding travel time compensation.

headings.title: Payment of party and witness interpreter fees from state appropriations
headings.reviewNote: Directs state payment of interpreter fees from appropriations when required by a party or witness in proceedings.

headings.title: Taxing interpreter costs to parties and pre-hearing deposit orders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court to tax fees as costs and require pre-hearing cash deposits in cases not covered by state payment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections governing reasonable interpreter/translator fees without travel-time pay, state payment for parties/witnesses, and party cost taxing/deposits.
